quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should be your main source of information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It tells you how to operate it, how to maintain it, and its specifications.

questions.question: What is the single most important thing you can do to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: What should you do in a no passing zone on a motorcycle?

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if the pass is completed before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is not allowed to pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: What is a benefit of smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle?

options.text: It can allow the rider to use engine braking.
It should not be done when other vehicles are nearby.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can allow the rider to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Engine braking through downshifting can help slow your motorcycle. If you do this, use your brake lights separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces can reduce traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
It catches the attention of other drivers.
It allows you to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot see, just like other vehicles. Always look over your shoulder to check for vehicles or hazards before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Why is riding alongside a car dangerous?

options.text: It can place you in a blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can place you in a blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous because you may end up in the driver's blind spot. The vehicle will also block your escape path.

questions.question: When should reflective clothing be worn?
questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing at all times to make yourself more visible. Most motorcycle accidents happen during the day, so bright clothing helps during daylight too.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.explanation: A face shield protects you from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and pebbles. It also protects your face during a crash.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up to increase distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If you can do so safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make the danger worse by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping a group of riders small?

options.text: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
A small group can ignore traffic laws.
Riders will always try to catch up to the group.
It will be hard to track where everyone is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A small group stays together better in traffic than a large group.
questions.explanation: Small groups have several advantages. Other vehicles can pass them more safely. They are less likely to be separated by traffic or stop lights. Slower riders do not have to rush to keep up.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Good protection includes a DOT helmet, eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, ankle-high boots, and durable gloves. A baseball cap does not provide protection.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, stopped at an intersection, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: Which of these is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, paint markings, and metal covers are slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: An approved helmet should:

options.text: Allow you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Reflective material on your helmet:

options.text: Should only be used at night.
Does not help you be seen.

questions.explanation: Reflective material on a vest or helmet makes you more visible to other drivers. Use it day and night.

questions.question: For best protection, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Cover your arms and legs completely.
Be loose and flap in the wind.
Only partially cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should completely cover your arms and legs. They should fit snugly but allow you to move freely. Leather or synthetic materials offer the best protection in an accident.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that helps other drivers see you and your motorcycle. Bright, reflective clothing makes it easier for others to spot you on the road.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not tell the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders. It should have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as you do.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: As much as a face shield

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not your whole face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What should boots or shoes do to protect you best?

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose
Cover your ankle and provide support

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover your ankle and provide support
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they do not catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What helps reduce the risk of head or neck injury in a crash?

options.text: Not allowing a passenger on the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the best way to reduce the risk of head or neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, you should check all of the following except:

options.text: The air pressure in the tires

questions.explanation: Before getting on a motorcycle, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, and lights and signals. Paint damage is not a safety check.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright clothing to help other drivers see you. Choose clothes that are easy to see during the day and at night.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you
Look for chances to squeeze through traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up suddenly or if another vehicle comes toward you too fast.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop brakes from working on dry roads
Warn you when brake pads need replacing

questions.explanation: ABS prevents skidding and wheel lock-up when you brake hard in a straight line. When electronic sensors detect a wheel is about to lock, the system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep the best braking power.
